Stop leaves the row saying stopped, the speed graph shows up, and the phrase screen has a way out.

## 🐞 Fixed

- **Stop left every row saying "running" for ever, and that was a real defect rather than a display one.** The app wrote a status when it paused a *waiting* task and none when it paused a *running* one, trusting the backend to report the new state. Some backends do; the download engine does not. So a task the engine was driving really did stop, the bar really did freeze, and the row still said running. It showed up with TorBox because a TorBox download hands its direct URL to the engine and then delegates the pause to it, inheriting exactly that gap — the defect was never TorBox's, it was in every path that ends at the engine. A state the app *commanded* is the app's to record.
- **The phrase screen has a back button.** Android's hardware key worked while nothing on screen did, which is a way out only if you already know it is there.
- **Every back button is a real glyph**, not the "‹" character — a typographic quotation mark borrowed as an icon, rendering at the font's weight rather than the badge's, with no shaft. The design language names a proper one.
- **The speed graph appears whenever something is queued**, not only while bytes are moving. The old rule was right for an empty instance and wrong for exactly the case worth looking at: a queue that says "running" while nothing moves. There, a line flat at zero is the answer.
- **The mark and the name in the overview sit together.** An adaptive icon's foreground layer carries a safe zone, about a quarter of the box on each side transparent by specification, and a gap measures the box rather than the ink — so a gap of 10 read as 21.

## 🔄 Changed

- **The About card carries the new wording, its version numbers link to their release pages, and the "report it" button has left the Problems card.**
